title: A still can't replace a performance
statement: Don't let a held picture stand in for a performed passage, because a still in its place changes what the passage is.
detail: The video tool's style research found a long passage of a performer speaking in its sampled reference and judged that replacing it with a held painting would change its character (`g9/tools/unit-video-essay/INTEGRATION.md`). Its pilot uses paintings only as local stand-ins and has no performer footage (`g9/tools/unit-video-essay/README.md`), and the lesson engine leaves its verse-over-footage frame unused until approved footage exists (`g9/transformer/README.md`).
against: It is a judgment from sampled frames, not a measured effect: the research says its "observations below describe sampled frames, not every transition." (g9/tools/unit-video-essay/INTEGRATION.md line 3).

evidence.quote: The sampled reference includes a long speaking-performer passage; replacing that passage with a held painting would change its character.
The example uses G9 paintings as stand-ins and has no performer footage.
